<description>
Verifies that reloading a wallet with load_on_startup=True when it is already in the startup list correctly evaluates to SKIP_WRITE and does not emit a warning under -nosettings.

This improves test coverage for the dynamic settings logic introduced in [#36176](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36176) by ensuring the C++ short-circuit logic properly evaluates the action type before checking the settings path.

This specific edge case was suggested by contributor jeanpablojp [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36176#discussion_r3944837660).
</description>

diff --git a/test/functional/wallet_startup.py b/test/functional/wallet_startup.py
index ed07bb044a..529fcb3441 100755
--- a/test/functional/wallet_startup.py
+++ b/test/functional/wallet_startup.py
@@ -81,6 +81,11 @@ class WalletStartupTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         assert_equal(node.loadwallet(filename="no_settings"), {"name": "no_settings"})
         assert_equal(node.get_wallet_rpc("no_settings").getwalletinfo()["walletname"], "no_settings")
 
+        # Re-adding a wallet already in the startup list skips the write, so it does not warn either.
+        assert_equal(node.unloadwallet(wallet_name="no_settings"), {})
+        assert_equal(node.loadwallet(filename="no_settings", load_on_startup=True), {"name": "no_settings"})
+        assert_equal(node.get_wallet_rpc("no_settings").getwalletinfo()["walletname"], "no_settings")
+
         assert_equal(node.loadwallet(filename="w2", load_on_startup=True), {"name": "w2", "warnings": [load_message]})
         assert_equal(set(node.listwallets()), {'', 'no_settings', 'w2'})
 

</patch>
